newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 3.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* The Dow Jones industrials fell by 94.04 points to 6517.01 and other indicators also declined as investors remained watchful about rates and earnings.
* Some analysts who follow IBM are lowering their forecasts for the company's first and second quarter profit as well as for the full year.
* The U.S. Federal Communications Commission is set to give broadcasters free digital-TV licenses after the companies agreed to launch the service in 10 cities by October 1998.
* Bank regulators reprimanded J.P. Morgan over management of its base-metals business related the bank's relationship with Sumitomo Corp.
* Factory orders in February rose 0.8 percent.
* H&R Block said it was in talks regarding a "business combination" for its CompuServe unit following reports America Online was considering a bid.
* Clayton, Dubilier & Rice's leveraged buyout of Riverwood RVW.N has come upon hard times.
* The announcement that reserves at Bre-X Mineral's gold field might be overstated has caused small mineral exploration companies to pull back new financings.
* Digital Equipment is considering consolidating its manufacturing facilities.
* Toyota Motor took legal steps to block Republic Industries from buying its car dealerships.
* Concerns over Phar-Mor's weak stock price were part of the reason a proposed merger between Phar-Mor and ShopKo was cancelled.
* Patriot American is in talks to buy Carnival Hotels in a deal valued at about $700 million.
* Waban backed out of a proposed deal with Kmart to divest their home-improvement store chains.
* General Motors light vehicle sales rose 4.1 percent in March compared to a year ago.

* Heard on the street: Hear that chipping sound? It's the sound of some analysts on Wall Street whittling away at earnings estimates for International Business Machines -- not just for the first and second quarter but for all of 1997.
* Credit markets: The Treasury said it would offer $8 billion of its new inflation-indexed securities next week, exceeding the size of the notes' $7 billion debut offer in January.
